newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Canal Plus sees big profit on Kirch deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Canal Plus sees big profit on Kirch deal.

text.p: French pay television group Canal Plus on Friday signed a key asset swap deal with Kirch Gruppe of Germany and said it expected a profit on the deal of some three billion francs ($500 million).
Under the pact, Canal Plus is selling its 37.5 percent stake in Germany's Premiere to Kirch while it is buying the German group's 45 percent stake in Italy's Telepiu.
Finance director Laurent Perpere told Reuters that the group now expected to post a 1997 net profit of close to three billion francs, provided corporate taxation remained unchanged in France.
"We could expect a net profit of close to three billion francs at unchanged tax rates," Perpere said by telephone.

The group had previously expected only to break even in 1997 due to losses at the NetHold operations it acquired earlier this year. Financial analysts were expecting some 600 million francs in losses from Nethold in Canal Plus' 1997 results.
The share market welcomed the deal, of which the outline was unveiled on Wednesday after a Canal Plus supervisory board meeting.
The shares traded two percent higher at 1,245 francs at 0939 and had opened at 1,253, close to their year-high of 1,258.
Canal Plus shares have been rising strongly since the beginning of June, when they stood at 973 francs, on expectations of a deal with Kirch.
Premiere was started in 1991 as a three-way joint-venture of Canal Plus, Kirch and Bertelsmann AG. It has now reached break-even and has more than 1.4 million digital subscribers.

"Our stake in Premiere is valued at some $600 million or between 3.8 and 3.9 billion francs. That compares with accumulated losses of close to 600 million francs. We have invested some 600 million and six years later we get 3.9 billion," Perpere said.

Telepiu was founded in 1989 by Silvio Berlusconi and some partners. He was later joined by Kirch and NetHold, then controlled by Richemont SA and MCL-Multi Choice Ltd which have since become large Canal Plus shareholders.
Canal Plus, after its merger with Nethold, had a 45 percent stake in Telepiu which will rise to 90 percent. Berlusconi's Fininvest Spa has the remainder.
Canal Plus said it would sell a large part of the Kirch stake in Telepiu to Italian partners.
"It is no secret that we are talking to Stet and RAI as well as with some other potential partners," Perpere said, referring to the Italian telecommunications company and state-run television group.
Perpere said that while the capital gain on Premiere would be taken into the 1997 results, the acquisition of the Telepiu stake did not enter in the results.

"In accounting terms the acquisition of the Telepiu stake has no effect on the results. There will be cash out on the balance sheet and a rise in the value of financial participation for the same amount," he said.
Canal Plus said that it and Kirch had used the figure of $1,250 per subscriber for the valuation of both Premiere and Telepiu.
"The market had been giving a value of beteen 3,230 and 4,250 francs per subscriber for Premiere, this deal puts the value at 7,735 francs per subscriber" said an analyst in Paris.
Using the subscriber figure, Premiere would be worth some $1.875 billion and Telepiu $1.0 billion.
"The only disappointment is that the value of Telepiu comes out lower than at the time of the merger with NetHold," another analyst said.
Canal Plus said that the deal allowed it to focus its investments in France, Spain, Italy and Scandinavia.
While Germany is Europe's biggest television market, Canal Plus said Italy was Europe's "most promising pay-television market."

Canal Plus had originally been a prime mover behind establishing digital television services in Germany, building on its technical know-how obtained in France, with Bertelsmann. Kirch had a rival project.
Last Wednesday, Kirch, Bertelsmann and Deutsche Telekom teamed up to provide digital television in Germany. Canal Plus bowed out.
"If we had stayed in Germany among Kirch, Bertelsmann and Deutsche Telekom, I don't think we would have had much to say," Perpere said.
-- Marcel Michelson, William Emmanuel and Denis Thomas, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452. ($ = 5.9 French Francs)
